1. [LDET.5.4] **The terminal ordinal — the first key, and it is source
   order.** Each rule is assigned a zero-based ordinal from the order its
   terminal appears in the compiled artefact, which `[RLOW.14.3]` requires
   to be canonical source order: within a file, the rule written first;
   across files, **import-DAG topological order, leaf libraries first**.

   Import-DAG rather than lexicographic-by-path because a path-based rule
   moves when a file is renamed, and because a library's rules are already
   loaded before its importer's — the DAG order is the one the compiler
   has, not one it would have to reconstruct.

   **This is spatial author intent** ([LDET.5.7.3]) and it is the reason
   the order is spec-defined rather than implementation-defined
   ([LTES.12.9]): a firing order that fell out of when matches happened to
   complete would depend on propagation internals, which is precisely what
   that clause forbids.

idris.name: ldet_5_1__select_next
idris.note: The outer key is the rule's position in source order; nothing else separates two rules.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__select_agree
idris.note: Both engines select the lowest ordinal with a pending activation: the first key, source order, on both sides.
